claims.text: ITS OWN SUMMARY, VERBATIM, and what it claims is a possibility and not a result: 'The idea that a sufficiently advanced technology may interact with, and acquire direct control over, the higher dimensions is a tantalizing possibility, and one that is most certainly worthy of deeper investigation. Control of this higher dimensional space may be a source of technological control over the dark energy density and could ultimately play a role in the development of exotic propulsion technologies; specifically, a warp drive. Of course, this may not be actualized until many years in the future...' Its closing sentence: '...if we may make predictions based on the innovative history of scientific pioneers of the past, then it seems entirely possible that the creative minds of the future may indeed find ways to accomplish what, to us, may seem like magic.'

claims.text: IT PRINTS THE REQUIREMENT AS A NUMBER, IN TWO TABLES. Table 2, 'Negative Energy Required for Warp Bubble (Larger Negative Energy)', and Table 3 after the reduction the paper argues for. At 0.01c: -3.03 x 10^46 J and -1.00 x 10^38 J. At 0.5c: -7.59 x 10^49 J and -2.50 x 10^41 J. AT LIGHT SPEED: -3.03 x 10^50 J and -1.00 x 10^42 J. At twice light speed: -1.21 x 10^51 J and -4.00 x 10^42 J. The document states that on its model 'energy requirements are reduced immensely when compared to the calculations of Lobo and Visser' and that 'All calculations are order-of-magnitude'.

Classical and Quantum Gravity, vol. 11, 1994, pp. L73-L77.' Its introduction states that 'a 1994 paper by Miguel Alcubierre placed the idea on a more solid theoretical footing'. THE DOCUMENT CLAIMS NO EXPERIMENT, NO APPARATUS AND NO OBSERVATION, and a DIA cover page and document number do not change that.
